title: Patient Financial Account Discount Terms by Financial Class
content:
The group offers two discounts on a Patient Financial Account, and their figures depend on the financial class. The prompt-pay discount is a percentage taken off a charge when the patient pays that charge's full remaining balance within the prompt-pay window, counted in calendar days from the posting date of the charge, provided the remaining balance is at least the prompt-pay minimum. The self-pay discount is a percentage taken off the gross fee-schedule charge of a self-pay service at posting. A rate of 0.00 percent means the discount is not offered on that class.

| Financial class (tier) | Prompt-pay discount (%) | Prompt-pay window (calendar days) | Prompt-pay minimum remaining balance (USD) | Self-pay discount (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | 0.00 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| Self-Pay Account | 15.00 | 30 | 50.00 | 35.00 |
| Medicare Part B Account | 0.00 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| Medicare Advantage Account | 0.00 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | 5.00 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | 5.00 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account | 7.50 | 30 | 100.00 | 0.00 |

## Points of the terms

- The self-pay discount rate is above zero on the Self-Pay Account alone, at 35.00 percent.
- The prompt-pay discount is offered at 15.00 percent on the Self-Pay Account, 7.5 percent on the High-Deductible Health Plan Account and 5.00 percent on the two commercial HMO/EPO and PPO/POS classes; it is not offered on the Medicaid Managed Care, Medicare Part B or Medicare Advantage accounts.
- The window is 30 calendar days on every class; the minimum remaining balance is 50.00 on the Self-Pay Account and 100.00 on every other class.

## Hypothetical selection case

A charge with a remaining balance of 80.00 (an illustrative figure) meets the 50.00 minimum on the Self-Pay Account but falls short of the 100.00 minimum on the Commercial PPO/POS Account; the same 80.00 charge on the Medicare Advantage Account earns nothing whatever its size, because the rate there is 0.00.
